youtube.title: Three Mile Island Had Already Happened Once, 18 Months Earlier. Nobody Passed On the Warning.
youtube.description:
On 28 March 1979, a stuck valve at Three Mile Island's Reactor 2 let cooling water escape while a control-room light said it was closed. Operators turned down the emergency cooling, and about half the core melted. In September 1977, a reactor from the same manufacturer at Davis-Besse in Ohio had the same stuck valve and the same operator mistake. Engineers warned that operators needed clearer instructions. The warning never reached them. The President's Commission found that heeding it could have prevented the accident.

📂 Case File #052: Three Mile Island

Sources: Report of the President's Commission on the Accident at Three Mile Island (Kemeny Commission), 'The Role of the Managing Utility and Its Suppliers' https://www.pddoc.com/tmi2/kemeny/utility_and_its_suppliers.htm ; MIT Technology Review, "Notes on a Meltdown" (2009) https://www.technologyreview.com/2009/10/20/29466/notes-on-a-meltdown/
Images: public domain (US government); Davis-Besse CC0.
